name: synthetic-sample
note: Synthetic conversation in the format of the private evaluation files: a long line with a question in the middle, a question cut in two by a pause, rhetorical and tag questions, a question for another person, a request to do something, short replies from You.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: Great, thanks for joining today. I wanted to talk a little bit about the application you sent us last week, so I was having a look at your background and your previous projects, but maybe you can just tell me a little bit more about yourself.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: And what particularly interests you in this team? And also in working on distributed systems in general.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Sure. I studied computer science and spent three years building mobile apps, and recently I moved towards backend work.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: That is why this team caught my eye.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: I guess one question I had was, you know, you are coming from a slightly different area than the one this team works in. Mostly front-end and mobile applications. As far as I can see, um, what.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: Is your motivation to move into a slightly different field? Again, this role is a bit like the infrastructure work you mentioned, but at a much larger scale. So what's your motivation there?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Well, actually.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: I like problems where the system has to stay correct under load, and I want to go deeper into that.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: The project that I have in mind. Maybe it's helpful if I give a little overview of what we are building, and then you can tell me if this is aligned with where you want to go. We have a large cache in front of the database. How do we know what to keep in it? That is the whole problem, right? Have you worked with Redis before? Because for this project that is probably the most useful experience, and I can explain how we use it if you have not.

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes, I used Redis for session storage and rate limiting.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: Okay. Maria, do you have any questions?

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: Yes. Can you go back to the second slide?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: So you said you used a queue between the two services, right?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: Why did you choose a queue there?

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: And how many messages per second did it handle?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: Mm.

lines.speaker: Them
lines.text: So that's roughly the plan. Does that sound good to you? And was there any other question that you had?

lines.speaker: You
lines.text: No, that's all. Thank you.
